# THE LÖWDIN CHALLENGE — THE OUTSIDE LITERATURE

*Compiled 2026-08-11 by live search. Every claim here is attributed; where a
paper's own abstract states a limitation, that limitation is quoted in substance
rather than softened. Nothing in this file is a result of this work.*

---

## 1 · THE CHALLENGE AS POSED

**Löwdin, P.-O. (1969).** *Some comments on the Periodic System of Elements.*
Int. J. Quantum Chem. Symp. **IIIS**, 331–334. Points out that the Madelung
(n+ℓ, n) rule has not been derived from quantum mechanics. This became "the
Löwdin challenge."

**Klechkovskii, V. M. (1951).** *(n+ℓ) groups in successive filling of atomic
electron configurations.* Doklady Akademii Nauk **80**, 603–606. The rule's
Russian originator; proposed an explanation in 1962. **Madelung, E. (1936).**
*Die Mathematischen Hilfsmittel des Physikers*, 3rd ed., p. 359. And earlier
still, **Janet (1928/1929)**, whose left-step table is the rule made a table —
unrecognised until Stewart (2010), which is why it carries Madelung's name.

---

## 2 · THE PRINCIPAL ATTEMPT, AND THE OBJECTION TO IT

**Demkov, Yu. N. & Ostrovsky, V. N. (1971/72).** *(n+ℓ) filling rule in the
Periodic System and focusing potentials.* Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. **62**, 125–132
[Sov. Phys. JETP **35**, 66–69, 1972].

The potential **U(r) ∝ −r⁻¹(r + R)⁻²** — a "focusing" potential closely
resembling the Thomas–Fermi potential — produces **additional degeneracy for
levels with identical N = n + ℓ at energy E = 0**. This is the closest thing in
the literature to a derivation, and it is what most later work builds on or
argues against. Related: Ostrovsky (2001, 2003) on what physics contributes to
the periodic law; Rosu *et al.* (1995) on the supersymmetry of the DO potentials;
the κ = ½ member of the family is the one obeying Madelung, κ = 1 being the
Maxwell fish-eye.

**THE OBJECTION.** Thyssen & Ceulemans (*Shattered Symmetry*, OUP 2017) conclude
that although the Demkov–Ostrovsky results reproduce the Madelung rule correctly,
**the way they were obtained cannot be considered a solution of the Löwdin
challenge — because the effective potential was GUESSED.** Kholodenko & Kauffman
(2019) make the same point: DO obtained correct results without rigorous
justification of the potential.

*This objection applies with equal force to any posited ordering functional,
including ν. See §6.*

---

## 3 · THE OTHER CLAIMANTS

**Allen, L. C. & Knight, E. T. (2002/2003).** *The Löwdin challenge: Origin of
the n+ℓ, n (Madelung) rule…* Int. J. Quantum Chem. **90**, 80–88. Treats the
table as an s/p framework internally perturbed by d and f electrons; a
perturbation operator locates the blocks; verified against Desclaux's 1973
Dirac–Fock calculations for Z = 1–118. **Scerri's commentary (2006) concludes the
explanation is inadequate on several grounds.**

**Kholodenko, A. L. & Kauffman, L. H. (2019); Kholodenko (2020).** *How the
modified Bertrand theorem explains regularities of the periodic table* (arXiv
1906.05278) and *…Regularities and Anomalies…* (arXiv 2002.12128). Uses Perlick's
extension of Bertrand's theorem to static spherically symmetric spacetimes
supporting closed orbits; shows the Tietz-type Schrödinger equation (Tietz 1956)
describes quantum motion in Bertrand spacetimes; claims an **analytic solution of
the Löwdin challenge.**

**Their own stated limitation:** the solution is **not universal** — the Madelung
exceptions among transition metals, lanthanides and actinides are **not described
in detail**, though they argue the method is capable of it.

**Group-theoretic approaches.** Kibler (2007), SO(4,2) ⊗ SU(2). Fet (2016),
Varlamov (2018). Thyssen (2013 dissertation) and Thyssen & Ceulemans (2017, 2020)
— SO(4,2) broken to the anti-de Sitter SO(3,2) explains period doubling, and the
Madelung rule is **rationalised via nonlinear Lie algebras reflecting the
screening of the Coulomb hole**. A 2026 arXiv preprint extends this to SO(4,4)
double towers. These approaches generally require some empirical input
(Ostrovsky's own assessment).

**Tangour, B. (2015).** *Beyond the Madelung–Klechkowski rule.* World J. Chem.
Educ. **3**(6), 160–167. Proposes a descriptor **K(ZX) built from all four
quantum numbers n, ℓ, mℓ, ms of the most recently added electron**, incrementing
with Z, claiming **no exceptions remain**, and connecting it to the first
ionisation energy. *Closest in spirit to putting the occupancy inside the
ordering functional.*

---

## 4 · THE DISSENTING POSITION

**Schwarz, W. H. E.** (and Cao, Hu, Li, Schwarz, *Pure Appl. Chem.* **91**,
1969–1999, 2019; Schwarz & Rich 2010). Argues the Madelung rule **does not truly
reflect the order of orbital occupation** in the way generally believed. The
(n+ℓ, n) rule was originally used by spectroscopists to remember which
*differentiating* orbital is added in free neutral atoms as Z increases; chemical
educators then applied it to ions, where it is a different claim. **The rule
usually fails where d and f orbitals are involved.**

*This is the objection that bears most directly on this work's own results: the
walk is precisely the neutral-atom differentiating-orbital reading, and its
failures are concentrated in d and f contests.*

---

## 5 · THE FIELD'S CONSENSUS

**Scerri, E. R. (2020).** *Recent attempts to change the periodic table.* Phil.
Trans. R. Soc. A **378**, 20190300. States that **numerous authors claim to have
met the challenge, but the generally held opinion is that no such derivation has
succeeded in the way Löwdin intended.**

Scerri was for many years the leading proponent of the "not derived" position and
has more recently said he has **somewhat changed his mind** (Inference Review,
2021). Others hold that the rule is empirical and that a first-principles
derivation would be surprising, and that obtaining configurations from first
principles is "a mathematical experiment rather than a mathematical deduction."

**So the challenge is open by consensus, with two live claimants (Bertrand
spacetimes; group theory) and one standing objection to the premise (Schwarz).**

---

## 6 · ATTRIBUTION OF THE 2026-08-11 "BRIDGE" FINDINGS

*Searched specifically to test whether the connections found in this session are
already in the literature. THEY LARGELY ARE, and the attributions are older and
more explicit than the session's claims assumed. Recorded here so that nothing
downstream repeats them as new.*

**The coordinates are not ours.** Demkov & Ostrovsky (1972) write the E = 0
degeneracy condition as **N − 1 = n_r + 2ℓ, where n_r = n − ℓ − 1 is the radial
quantum number** — the node count. Belokolos (2017) states it as an identity:

> **M = n + ℓ = n_r + 2ℓ + 1**

So the pair (node count, angular momentum) is the standard coordinate system of
this literature, not a discovery of this work. That ν's radicand is built from
n − ℓ − 1 places it in the same variables the field has used since 1972.

**The period-2 structure in N is not ours either.** Belokolos gives the period
lengths in closed form:

> **L_M = 2( ⌊M/2⌋ + 1 )²**, yielding 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32, …

The floor function ⌊M/2⌋ IS the period-two structure. The session's observation —
that (n, ℓ) → (n+1, ℓ+1) leaves n − ℓ − 1 and Δn invariant while raising N by
two, so the crossing sets repeat with period two — is a restatement of the same
arithmetic in a different object. It is correct and it is not new.

**The odd/even N split** appears in the Rumer–Fet / SO(4,2) line: the SO(4,4)
double-tower construction marks rings of odd n+ℓ separately, and the "doubling of
the representation space" is the same parity distinction.

**What this session's search did NOT find in the literature.** No source located
reports (i) the corridor construction — an interval L(Z) < a < U(Z) on a carried
ordering parameter, with endpoints as exact surds in node counts; (ii) a
falsification test of the ordering form against a case where the corridor is
EMPTY, as the nuclear shell ordering is; or (iii) an out-of-sample or
forward-horizon measurement of a proposed rule against a Madelung null.
**Absence from these searches is not absence from the literature**, and (i) in
particular should be searched again with better terms before any claim is made.

**The corrected reading of the "bridge".** This work has independently arrived at
the coordinate system the field has used for fifty years. That is a validation of
the coordinates and it makes comparison possible — it is not a contribution.
Belokolos additionally states an intention to compare his spectra against the
NIST Atomic Spectra Database, which is the same test this work has been running.

---

## 7 · WHERE THIS WORK SITS

**Different in kind.** Every attempt above seeks a POTENTIAL or a SYMMETRY GROUP
from which the n+ℓ ordering follows. This work posits an ordering functional
directly — ν(n, ℓ, q) = n − a√(n−ℓ−1 + q/2(2ℓ+1)) — and tests it by whether the
resulting corridor is non-empty at each element.

**The guessed-potential objection applies to ν too**, and must be answered rather
than dodged. The answer available here is not that ν is derived but that it is
FALSIFIABLE in a way a guessed potential is not: the same corridor construction
applied to the nuclear shell ordering gives an EMPTY feasible set (registers
1367–1371, 1394), while the atomic corridor is non-empty at 106 of 106. A form
that can fail and does not is a different epistemic object from a form fitted to
succeed. *That is a defence of the method, not a derivation of ν.*

**Points of contact worth pursuing.**

- Demkov–Ostrovsky locate their content at **degeneracy at E = 0 for equal
  N = n+ℓ**. This work locates its content at **crossings** — the values of a
  where two orderings become indistinguishable, the nineteen surds. Both say the
  physics lives where the ordering is degenerate. Whether these are the same
  degeneracy in two languages is a concrete question and has not been asked.
- Tangour's K(ZX) puts the occupancy of the newly added electron into the
  descriptor; ν puts q into the radicand as the Pauli fraction q/cap. Two
  attempts to remove the exceptions by carrying occupancy. **His claim of no
  exceptions should be checked against our 93 of 100.**
- Schwarz's objection predicts failures concentrated in d and f. Ours are: Mn,
  Tc, Gd, Cm are all s-vs-d or d-vs-f contests, and the half-capacity mechanism
  is a d and f phenomenon. **The objection and our miss classification agree**,
  which is either a confirmation of his reading or a symptom of the same cause.

**What appears NOT to be in the literature.** No source found reports an
**out-of-sample generation test against a Madelung null**. The claimants ask
whether the rule FOLLOWS from their formalism; none appears to ask how far past
the record their formalism can DERIVE, or to score it against plain Madelung
run under identical conditions. This work has measured that:

    conditional, one step ahead      law 90 · Madelung 96   (of 106)
    free-running from hydrogen       law 72 · Madelung 94
    forward horizon from a prefix    law mean 3.9 · Madelung mean 6.0 steps

**On that measurement the law currently loses to the rule it seeks to explain.**
That is a negative result, but the MEASUREMENT is the thing not previously made,
and it converts the challenge from a yes/no into a distance.

---

## 8 · THE MATHEMATICS THE CORRIDOR BELONGS TO

*Found 2026-08-11 when the person named the object: an old-school question about
ranked order pairs. It is, and it is not in the chemistry literature at all.*

The corridor asks whether an observed ranked order is **additively representable**
by a candidate form. Each adjacent pair gives one strict linear inequality in the
parameters; the order is representable iff the system is feasible; and an
infeasible system has a **Farkas certificate**, called in this literature a
**CANCELLATION CONDITION**.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kraft, Pratt & Seidenberg (1959)** | *Intuitive probability on finite sets*, Ann. Math. Statist. **30**, 408–419. De Finetti's conjecture disproved: a five-element comparative probability order satisfying every obvious condition and admitting no representing measure. The founding counterexample. |
| **Scott (1964)** | *Measurement structures and linear inequalities*, J. Math. Psych. **1**, 233–247. The general criterion, proved by linear programming. |
| **Krantz, Luce, Suppes & Tversky (1971)** | *Foundations of Measurement* I. Farkas' lemma **alone** yields the cancellation law as the characterisation of additively representable relations. |
| **Fishburn (1996a,b,c; 1997)** | How high the cancellation order must climb before infeasibility appears. **The standing warning: feasibility checked at low order is NOT representability.** |
| **Motzkin (1936) · Kuhn (1956)** | Solvability and consistency for linear inequalities — the machinery underneath. |

**WHERE THIS WORK'S TWO CORRIDORS SIT.**

- **Atomic, ν's family** — 106 of 106 corridors non-empty, but that is **106
  separate one-dimensional feasibility results, not one system.** Solved as one
  system the table is **INFEASIBLE**: the running intersection empties fourteen
  times. **Each element's local order is representable; the table is not, by any
  single parameter** (R 1310, 1409, 1463). In dimension one Helly's theorem makes
  pairwise feasibility global, so nothing hides — the infeasibility is plain.
- **Nuclear, Nilsson's family** — infeasible. The six constraint vectors are all
  positive multiples of (4, 1), so the constraint matrix has **RANK ONE**, and
  three point each way. The certificate is a **second-order cancellation**, the
  shortest such a system can have — where KPS's counterexample needs a higher one.

**AND THE FIELD REACHES THE SAME ANSWER BY FITTING.** arXiv 1110.6134 Table I
gives κ = 0.0250 for ℓ = 1 within N = 5 where ℓ = 3 and ℓ = 5 get 0.0570 — a
factor of 2.3 inside one shell. ℓ-independence abandoned empirically, which is
what the rank-one certificate says is forced. Two routes to one answer.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE METHOD.** The corridor is not a new instrument; it is a
classical one, and naming it imports its theorems and its warnings. Any future
corridor must be SOLVED as a system rather than spot-checked, because Fishburn
shows low-order feasibility can hide high-order infeasibility.

---

## 9 · WHAT TO READ NEXT, IN ORDER

0. **Belokolos 2017 (SIGMA 13, 038; arXiv 1706.02535)** — READ FIRST. States
   M = n + ℓ = n_r + 2ℓ + 1 and L_M = 2(⌊M/2⌋+1)² explicitly, which between them
   attribute this session's coordinate and period-two findings. Also proposes
   comparing his spectra to the NIST ASD, which is this work's own test.

1. **Demkov & Ostrovsky 1972** — READ (already fetched in full). Their E = 0
   degeneracy at fixed n_r + 2ℓ is the parent of everything above. Whether their
   degeneracy is the same event as this work's CROSSINGS is the open question;
   the coordinates are shared, the construction is not.
2. **Kholodenko 2020 (arXiv 2002.12128)** — the most recent claimed solution;

3. **Thyssen & Ceulemans 2017, ch. 13** — contains a literature study of

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""onbank.py — what the FOLDER alone can answer about facets 1-5.

Source: /mnt/project/COORDINATES-2_13.csv (grade == 'measured' only).
No fetch. No computed-grade value is read as evidence.

Diagonal reading (bridge Finding II): on a Madelung diagonal M = n + l,
    p = n - l - 1 = M - 2l - 1.
So at fixed M the vector index p is determined by l alone, and the facet
inequalities of Finding I are second differences of the measured channel
defect read across l.
"""
import csv, sys

ROWS = list(csv.DictReader(open('/mnt/project/COORDINATES-2_13.csv', encoding='utf-8')))
MEAS = {}
for r in ROWS:
    if r['grade'] == 'measured':
        MEAS.setdefault((int(r['Z']), int(r['charge'])), {})[int(r['l'])] = float(r['delta'])

FACETS = {
    1: ((0, +1), (2, -2), (4, +1)),
    2: ((0, +2), (2, -3), (6, +1)),
    3: ((1, +1), (4, -2), (6, +1)),
    4: ((1, +1), (3, -2), (5, +1)),
    5: ((3, +1), (5, -2), (7, +1)),
}

def vvec(species, M):
    """v[p] from measured delta at diagonal M; p = M - 2l - 1."""
    d = MEAS.get(species, {})
    return {M - 2 * l - 1: v for l, v in d.items() if 0 <= M - 2 * l - 1 <= 7}

def evaluate(name, species, M, facets):
    v = vvec(species, M)
    print(f"\n{name}  (Z={species[0]}, charge={species[1]}, diagonal M={M})")
    print("  measured v[p]: " + ", ".join(f"v{p}={v[p]:.5f}" for p in sorted(v)) or "  none")
    for f in facets:
        need = [p for p, _ in FACETS[f]]
        have = [p for p in need if p in v]
        if len(have) == len(need):
            val = sum(c * v[p] for p, c in FACETS[f])
            print(f"  facet {f}  {val:+.5f}   {'SATISFIED (<0)' if val < 0 else 'VIOLATED (>=0)'}")
        else:
            miss = [p for p in need if p not in v]
            ls = [(M - 1 - p) // 2 for p in miss]
            print(f"  facet {f}  NOT EVALUABLE — missing v{miss} = measured delta at l={ls}")

print("=" * 68)
print("REPRODUCTION — M=7 diagonal, Xe core (bridge Finding III, facets 1-2)")
print("=" * 68)
evaluate("Cs I", (55, 1), 7, [1, 2])
evaluate("Ba II", (56, 2), 7, [1, 2])

print("\n" + "=" * 68)
print("THE M=8 DIAGONAL — facets 4 and 5, from the folder alone")
print("=" * 68)
for name, sp in [("Fr I", (87, 1)), ("Ra II", (88, 2)), ("Ac III", (89, 3)),
                 ("Tl I", (81, 1)), ("Hg II", (80, 2))]:
    evaluate(name, sp, 8, [4, 5])

print("\n" + "=" * 68)
print("FACET 3 — the cross-diagonal chord, on whatever carries v1,v4,v6")
print("=" * 68)
for name, sp in [("Tl I", (81, 1)), ("Fr I", (87, 1)), ("Cs I", (55, 1))]:
    evaluate(name, sp, 8, [3])

# WHAT THE FOLDER ANSWERS WITHOUT A FETCH

*M's instruction: review everything in the working project folder before fetching outside.
Computed by `onbank.py` and two inline scripts, from `COORDINATES-2_13.csv` (grade `measured`
only, 358 rows on 75 species). No fetch attempted. No computed-grade value read as evidence.
Nothing written to any index, register or artefact.*

---

## 0 · A convention audited before it was used

**`charge` in `COORDINATES.tsv` is 1-based — it is the SPECTRUM NUMBER, not the ion charge.**
charge = 1 is the neutral atom; Ra II is charge 2. My first pass queried charge = 0 for neutrals,
got zero rows, and was one keystroke from reporting *"Rb I, Fr I and Rn I are absent from the
index"* — a negative that would have been a statement about my query. R 1672's clause, fired.
The convention is consistent with the index's own arithmetic: charge runs 1…Z, so
Σ_{Z=1..120} Z = 7,260 pairs.

## 1 · The instrument reproduces

Bridge Finding III reported facets 1–2 at Cs I as −1.308, −3.281. Recomputed from
`COORDINATES-2_13.csv`: **−1.30781, −3.28301**. Ba II: −0.83270, −2.13390.

## 2 · THE DIAGONAL MAP MAKES FACETS 1 AND 4 ONE INEQUALITY

On a Madelung diagonal M = n + ℓ, p = n − ℓ − 1 = **M − 2ℓ − 1**, so ℓ alone fixes p and
consecutive ℓ steps p by two. Therefore:

| M parity | ℓ = 3, 2, 1, 0 maps to | facets living there |
|---|---|---|
| **M odd** (7) | p = 0, 2, 4, 6 | facets 1, 2 |
| **M even** (8) | p = 1, 3, 5, 7 | facets 4, 5 |

Written in the channel defects δ(ℓ) of one closed core:

    facet 1  =  facet 4  =  δ(f) − 2δ(d) + δ(p)
    facet 2  =            2δ(f) − 3δ(d) + δ(s)
    facet 5  =            δ(d) − 2δ(p) + δ(s)
    facet 3  =  the one chord that mixes parities — the cross-diagonal, as Finding II said

**Facets 1 and 4 are the same functional of the same four numbers, read on diagonals of
opposite parity.** Five facets, four distinct diagonal conditions.

**Consequence for the board.** Open item 2 read *"facets 4–5 UNTESTED — no measured d/f channel
for the Rn core."* Under the diagonal map, facets 4–5 need no Rn core: they need any species with
measured δ at ℓ = 0, 1, 2, 3. **The folder holds 43 such species.** The Rn-core instance is a
separate question and remains open; the facets themselves are not blocked on it.

## 3 · Facets 4 and 5, measured — 43 species

    facet 1 / facet 4   satisfied 10 / 43
    facet 2             satisfied 13 / 43
    facet 5             satisfied 31 / 43

Hg II carries all four channels and satisfies both M=8 facets: **facet 4 −0.86980,
facet 5 −0.57840** (v₁ 1.06220 · v₃ 2.87580 · v₅ 3.81960 · v₇ 4.18500, all four n inside the
compendium's stated n-ranges for that species).

**The 10/43 is a POOLED number and must not be read as a rate.** The population contains two
domains — hydrogenic light species where δ(d) and δ(f) are both ≈ 0, and heavy species where the
d channel has collapsed. Finding III's five cores are all of the second kind. Pooling them is the
operation this project forbids.

## 4 · Where facet 1/4 is satisfied, the d channel has collapsed

    facet 1/4 SATISFIED (n=10)   δ(d) median 1.8942   range 0.0014 – 2.8758
    facet 1/4 VIOLATED  (n=33)   δ(d) median 0.0772   range 0.0002 – 0.8917
    best single threshold on δ(d): 41 / 43

The two misses are hydrogenic rows (Li III, Be IV) whose facet value is at the 10⁻⁴ level — they
satisfy by rounding, not by shape. The smallest δ(d) among true satisfiers is **0.6202 — Ti IV**,
which is the exact value `SPECTRA.md` §"The Janet collapse" uses as its own boundary example.

**Stated as measured, not as a condition.** This is an association on 43 species with a threshold
accuracy, and P1-FINDING §2 records what happens when an enrichment of this kind is promoted to a
condition. What it does is connect Finding I's facets to an object already in the compendium: the
collapse threshold is a **Janet block boundary read from the periodic table and not fitted**
(R 1657), so the facet condition may be carried by a coordinate the index already holds.

## 5 · What is genuinely missing, named exactly

| want | on disk | missing |
|---|---|---|
| Rn-core M=8 diagonal | **Fr I** measured δ(s) 5.07221, δ(p) 4.59521 | δ(d) → facet 5; δ(d)+δ(f) → facet 4 |
| Ra II, Ac III | 8 rows each, **all computed** | every measured channel |
| facet 3 at Tl I | δ(s) 4.75066, δ(d) 3.11838, δ(f) 1.03131 | δ(p) — computed grade only |

**Before any NIST call: the bank already holds `spectra_raw/queue2/FrI.tsv` (3,332 bytes),
`RaI.tsv`, `AcI.tsv`, `RnI.tsv`, `TlI.tsv`, `HgI.tsv`, `PbI.tsv`.** Fr I reached the index with
two channels of the four its raw table may contain — which is the FLAG 1 pattern exactly
(Rb I: captured at R 1258, promoted for Sr II, not for Rb I). **A missing index row is not
evidence of a missing measurement.** The next act is to read `FrI.tsv`, not to query ASD.

## 6 · Not read, and named rather than glossed

`REGISTER-2_13.txt` (13,543 lines) consulted by targeted query only — collapse, R 1699/1700,
entry count. `The_Method_1_6-10.pdf` is **UTF-8 text, 11,108 lines**, not a PDF (R 1702), and is
the book Parts II–VII that every bridge names as unread — it is present and extractable in this
chat. `The_Register-4.pdf` likewise, 12,032 lines. The four compendium files are **zip archives
of page rasters** and carry no extractable text. `SPECTRA-2_13.txt` §II read as a table
(596 channels, 105 species) and not line by line; §III–IV not read.

## Folder reviewed. The fetch is not yet warranted — and two facets were already answerable.

**Read in full:** both Löwdin bridges, `CHAPTER-LOWDIN.md` and `LOWDIN-LITERATURE.md` verbatim, `CLIQUE3-FINDING.md`, `P1-FINDING.md`, `BOARD-2`, `BOARD-3-REVISED`, `BRIDGE-1_8_3`, both certificates, both challenge statements, and the census of all 28 files. Read by shape: `SPECTRA` §II (596 channels, 105 species), the bank manifest (694 files), `COORDINATES` (104,832 rows), `STEPS` (524 rows), the code bundle (13 scripts). Named unread in §6 of the artefact.

### One convention audit that nearly became a false negative
`charge` is **1-based** — the spectrum number, not the ion charge. My first query asked for charge = 0 neutrals, got nothing, and was one step from reporting Rb I, Fr I and Rn I absent from the index. R 1672, fired on myself.

### The finding that moves the board
On a diagonal, p = M − 2ℓ − 1, so ℓ alone fixes p. Written in channel defects, **facet 1 and facet 4 are the same inequality** — δ(f) − 2δ(d) + δ(p) — read on diagonals of opposite parity. Five facets, four distinct diagonal conditions.

So facets 4–5 never needed the Rn core. They need any species with measured δ at ℓ = 0,1,2,3, and **the folder holds 43**. Hg II satisfies both: facet 4 −0.86980, facet 5 −0.57840. Cs I's facets 1–2 reproduce at −1.30781, −3.28301 against the bridge's −1.308, −3.281, so the instrument is checked before it is used.

The pooled counts (10/43 · 13/43 · 31/43) are **not rates** — the population spans hydrogenic species where δ(d) ≈ 0 and heavy species where the d channel has collapsed, and pooling those is what this project forbids. Split on δ(d), facet 1/4 satisfaction separates 41/43, and the smallest true satisfier is Ti IV at 0.6202 — the exact value `SPECTRA.md` uses as its own Janet-collapse boundary example. Stated as an association, not a condition; P1-FINDING §2 records what promoting an enrichment costs.

### Why not to call NIST yet
The bank holds `spectra_raw/queue2/FrI.tsv`, `RaI.tsv`, `AcI.tsv`, `RnI.tsv`, `TlI.tsv`. Fr I reached the index with two channels of the four its raw table may hold — the FLAG 1 pattern exactly. **A missing index row is not evidence of a missing measurement.** Facet 5 on the Rn core is one number away: δ(6d) for Fr I. The next act is to read `FrI.tsv`.

### The store already held it
`MEASUREMENTS.tsv` carries **three** Fr I series, not two — including ℓ = 2, δ 3.42371, 50 members, n 6–30. `COORDINATES.tsv` carries only ℓ = 0 and 1. **The d channel was measured, stored, and never promoted to the index** — FLAG 1's pattern, second instance. The bridge's "Fr I — unlikely in ASD" was a guess about a file that was on disk.

**Reproduction gate first:** all three series regenerate from `spectra_raw/queue2/FrI.tsv` through the project's own `store_gen.members()`, medians exact to five decimals, member counts 24/24 · 48/48 · 50/50.

### The measurement
On M = 8, p = 7 − 2ℓ, so facet 5 = δ(d) − 2δ(p) + δ(s):

    channel medians   -0.69450   SATISFIED
    diagonal points   -0.84816   SATISFIED   (6d, 7p, 8s individually)

### Facet 4 is a null, and it is in the world
`FrI.tsv` has **no f series and no g series at all** — s/p/d only to n = 30, stated in its own header. Not our gap; the data has not been published. `ISOLATE-LOWDIN-3.tar.gz` — **40 KB, 14 files, verified against its own manifest.** It carries the seven heavy-element level tables, the full store, `store_gen.py`, the 1,287 non-computed index rows, and this session's findings and script. `store_gen` runs with the isolate root as cwd. **No restore point is needed next session** — upload this instead of the 14 MB bank.

Refusal, per §2.9: a series that cannot be read is written with members_found=0
and a NAMED reason. It is never dropped.
"""
import re, csv, statistics as st, os

RINF = 109737.31568
AMU = 1822.888486
MASS = {5:('B',10.811), 11:('Na',22.98977), 13:('Al',26.98154), 22:('Ti',47.867),
        31:('Ga',69.723), 32:('Ge',72.630), 36:('Kr',83.798), 38:('Sr',87.62),
        39:('Y',88.90584), 40:('Zr',91.224), 49:('In',114.818), 50:('Sn',118.710),
        54:('Xe',131.293), 55:('Cs',132.905), 56:('Ba',137.327), 70:('Yb',173.045),
        71:('Lu',174.967), 72:('Hf',178.49), 80:('Hg',200.592), 81:('Tl',204.383),
        82:('Pb',207.2), 86:('Rn',222.018), 87:('Fr',223.020), 88:('Ra',226.025)}
LM = {'s':0,'p':1,'d':2,'f':3,'g':4,'h':5,'i':6,'k':7}

_cache = {}
def levels(sym):
    """Raw level rows for a neutral species. Header may be absent (19 of 61 files)."""
def outer(config):
    """The Rydberg electron's (n, l), or a named refusal.

    The config is a dot-joined chain; the last component is the outer electron
    in all four languages. What differs between languages is the DECORATION —
    jK and jj append <j> to the component and nest the parent in parentheses —
    so the decoration is stripped and the same shell is read underneath.
    Returns (n, l, None) or (None, None, reason).
    """
    c = config.strip()
    if not c:
        return None, None, 'config_empty'
    c = c.rstrip('?')
    c = re.sub(r'<[^>]*>', '', c)          # drop <j> on the component
    part = c.split('.')[-1]
    part = part.rstrip('?')
    if part.endswith(')'):                  # last component is a parent group
        return None, None, 'no_outer_electron'
    m = SHELL.search(part)
    if not m:
        return None, None, 'shell_unreadable'
    if m.group(3) and int(m.group(3)) > 1:
        return None, None, 'outer_occupancy_gt_1'
    return int(m.group(1)), LM[m.group(2)], None


def parent_of(config):
    """The printed parent: the last parenthesised group, decoration kept.
    R 1650 says AS PRINTED, so <j> is retained — 2P*<3/2> and 2P*<1/2> are
    different parents and the store records them as such."""
    g = re.findall(r'\(([^()]*)\)', config)
    return g[-1].strip() if g else ''


def members(sym, R, lim, L, term, parent):
    """delta(n) for every level of THIS series below the limit.
    The series is (l, term, parent). Where the store records no parent the
    parent condition is not applied — R 1664's 'no parent stated' is a bin of
    its own, not a filter with an empty argument."""
    out, refusals = [], []
    for r in levels(sym):
        if len(r) < 4:
            continue
        cfg = r[0].strip()
        if r[1].strip() != term:
            continue
        n, l, why = outer(cfg)
        if why:
            refusals.append(why)
            continue
        if l != L:
            continue
        if parent and parent_of(cfg) != parent:
            continue
        v = r[3].strip()
        br = v.startswith('[')
        try:
            E = float(v.strip('[]').replace('+', ''))
        except ValueError:
            refusals.append('energy_unparsed')
            continue
        if E >= lim:
            continue
        out.append((n, n - R ** 0.5 / ((lim - E) ** 0.5), br))
    return sorted(out), refusals

        term = r['term'].strip()
        parent = r['parent'].strip()
        stored = int(r['members'])
        base = [r['Z'], r['charge'], r['l'], r['mult'], term, parent,
                r['language'].strip(), r['n_lo'], r['n_hi'], stored]
        if Z not in MASS:
            out.append(base + [0, 'no'] + [''] * 8 + ['Z_not_in_mass_table'])
            refused += 1

        lim, lstat, llab = assign_limit(sym, parent, top_E)
        try:
            lim_stored = float(r['limit'])
        except ValueError:
            lim_stored = None
        agrees = ('yes' if (lim is not None and lim_stored is not None
                            and abs(lim - lim_stored) < 1e-3) else 'no')
        exceeds = ('yes' if (lim is not None and top_E is not None and top_E >= lim) else 'no')
        tail = [f'{lim:.5f}' if lim is not None else '', lstat, llab,
                f'{lim_stored:.5f}' if lim_stored is not None else '', agrees, exceeds]
        if lim is None:
            out.append(base + [0, 'no'] + [''] * 8 + [lstat] + tail)
            refused += 1

        pts, refs = members(sym, R, lim, int(r['l']), term, parent)
        if not pts:
            why = max(set(refs), key=refs.count) if refs else 'no_level_matched'
            out.append(base + [0, 'no'] + [''] * 8 + [why] + tail)
            refused += 1
            continue
        d = [p[1] for p in pts]
        ok = (len(pts) == stored)
        matched += ok
        med, mean, asym = st.median(d), st.mean(d), d[-1]
        if ok and abs(med - float(r['delta'])) < 1e-4:
            agree += 1
        out.append(base + [len(pts), 'yes' if ok else 'no', r['delta'],
                           f'{med:.5f}', f'{mean:.5f}', f'{asym:.5f}',
                           f'{max(d)-min(d):.5f}', sum(p[2] for p in pts),
                           'yes' if pts[-1][2] else 'no',
                           'usable' if not lstat.startswith('unwitnessed') else r['delta_status'],
                           ''] + tail)
    with open('MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv', 'w', newline='') as f:
        w = csv.writer(f, delimiter='\t')
        w.writerow(cols)
        w.writerows(out)

def levels(sym):
    """Raw level rows for a neutral species. Header may be absent (19 of 61 files)."""
    if sym in _cache: return _cache[sym]
    path = f'spectra_raw/queue2/{sym}I.tsv'
    if not os.path.exists(path): _cache[sym] = []; return []
    rows = [l.rstrip('\n\r').split('\t') for l in open(path, encoding='utf-8')
            if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
    if rows and 'onfig' in rows[0][0]: rows = rows[1:]
    _cache[sym] = rows
    return rows


SHELL = re.compile(r'(\d+)([spdfghik])(\d*)$')

# FACET 5 CLOSES ON THE Rn CORE — FROM THE BANK, WITHOUT A FETCH

*Bank `restore-point-2_13.tar.gz` verified by hash against `BANK-2_13-MANIFEST.txt`:
`8057709403ed2c795cc753f74e68b2cbfc3aeb9c67f45e7c0e38b3129fd857a5`, 708 entries
(694 files + 14 dirs). Ten files extracted, nothing else read. Nothing written to the
register, the store, `COORDINATES.tsv` or any generated artefact.*

---

## 1 · The premise of board item 2 was false, and the store says so

Bridge §9 item 2: *"Facets 4–5 by measurement. Needs measured d and f channels on the Rn core:
Fr I (unlikely in ASD), Ra II, Ac III."*

**`MEASUREMENTS.tsv` already holds Fr I's d channel.** Three Fr I series are in the store:

    Z=87 charge=1  l=0  2S   delta 5.07221  spread 0.10117  n  7–30  members 24
    Z=87 charge=1  l=1  2P*  delta 4.59521  spread 0.19183  n  7–30  members 48
    Z=87 charge=1  l=2  2D   delta 3.42371  spread 2.38116  n  6–30  members 50

`COORDINATES.tsv` carries **only ℓ = 0 and ℓ = 1** for Fr I as measured. **The d channel was
measured, stored, and never promoted to the index** — FLAG 1's pattern, second instance
(Rb I, R 1258, was the first). *A missing index row is not evidence of a missing measurement,
and "unlikely in ASD" was a guess where the file was on disk.*

## 2 · Reproduction gate — 3 of 3 series regenerate from raw

Recomputed with the project's own `store_gen.members()` from `spectra_raw/queue2/FrI.tsv`,
whose header quotes its `destination_url` from tool-result metadata. Limit 32,848.872 cm⁻¹
(Fr II 6p⁶ ¹S₀), assigned by `assign_limit` as *forced — sole published limit*.
R mass-corrected for ²²³Fr.

| ℓ | stored δ | recomputed median | members stored / found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5.07221 | **5.07221** | 24 / 24 |
| 1 | 4.59521 | **4.59521** | 48 / 48 |
| 2 | 3.42371 | **3.42371** | 50 / 50 |

Exact to five decimals on all three. The instrument is checked before it is used.

## 3 · FACET 5, MEASURED AT THE Rn CORE

On the M = 8 diagonal, p = M − 2ℓ − 1 = 7 − 2ℓ, so ℓ = 2, 1, 0 give p = 3, 5, 7 and
facet 5 = v₃ − 2v₅ + v₇ = δ(d) − 2δ(p) + δ(s).

| ℓ | diagonal n | p | δ at that n | channel median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 6d | 3 | 3.43035 | 3.42371 |
| 1 | 7p | 5 | 4.69260 | 4.59521 |
| 0 | 8s | 7 | 5.10670 | 5.07221 |

    facet 5, channel medians   -0.69450   SATISFIED (< 0)
    facet 5, diagonal points   -0.84816   SATISFIED (< 0)

**Two routes, same verdict** (§2.8). The channel-median route is the one Finding III used at
Cs I and Ba II; the diagonal-point route uses only the three levels the diagonal actually names.

**Facet 5 holds by measurement at the Rn core.** With Hg II (facet 4 −0.86980, facet 5 −0.57840)
and Cs I / Ba II on M = 7, the M = 8 pair is now half closed on the core the generating steps
Ac, Th, Cm, Lr actually sit on.

## 4 · FACET 4 IS A NULL, AND THE NULL IS IN THE WORLD

Facet 4 = v₁ − 2v₃ + v₅ needs δ(nf) at the Rn core. **`FrI.tsv` has no f series and no g series
at all** — its own header states s/p/d only, to n = 30, and the configurations confirm it.

This is not a refusal and not a gap in our reading. It is E measuring the *world*: the Fr I f
channel has not been published. The remaining one-electron Rn-core species are **Ra II** and
**Ac III**, and neither is in `spectra_raw` — `store_gen.levels()` reads neutrals only
(`queue2/{sym}I.tsv`), and the Z = 88 rows in the store are **Ra I**, whose Rydberg electron sees
a Ra⁺(7s) core, not Rn. *Ra I's f channel (δ 1.14629, n 5–8) must not be read as an Rn-core
value — that is the language/domain boundary this project forbids crossing.*

**So the fetch, if M rules for it, is now exactly specified and minimal: Ra II, for the nf series.**
It would also give an independent Rn-core check of s, p and d against Fr I.

## 5 · What is owed

- The Fr I d row's promotion to `COORDINATES.tsv` — **a ruling, not an act.** It is the same
  operation FLAG 1 asks for on Rb I, and *a write to COORDINATES is not complete until every
  artefact is regenerated and both gates rerun*.
- Register entries: facets 1 ≡ 4 under the diagonal map; the 43-species facet population and its
  two domains; the δ(d)-collapse association (41/43); facet 5 measured at the Rn core by two
  routes; facet 4 as a published-data null; the second promotion failure.

## Facet 5 closes on the Rn core — no fetch, and the fetch premise was wrong

**Bank verified by hash** against `BANK-2_13-MANIFEST.txt`: `805770940…d857a5`, 708 entries (694 files + 14 dirs). **Ten files extracted, nothing else read.** Nothing written to the bank.

### The store already held it
`MEASUREMENTS.tsv` carries **three** Fr I series, not two — including ℓ = 2, δ 3.42371, 50 members, n 6–30. `COORDINATES.tsv` carries only ℓ = 0 and 1. **The d channel was measured, stored, and never promoted to the index** — FLAG 1's pattern, second instance. The bridge's "Fr I — unlikely in ASD" was a guess about a file that was on disk.

**Reproduction gate first:** all three series regenerate from `spectra_raw/queue2/FrI.tsv` through the project's own `store_gen.members()`, medians exact to five decimals, member counts 24/24 · 48/48 · 50/50.

### The measurement
On M = 8, p = 7 − 2ℓ, so facet 5 = δ(d) − 2δ(p) + δ(s):

    channel medians   -0.69450   SATISFIED
    diagonal points   -0.84816   SATISFIED   (6d, 7p, 8s individually)

Two routes, one verdict. With Hg II's −0.86980 / −0.57840, the M = 8 pair is half closed on the core the generating steps Ac, Th, Cm and Lr actually sit on.

### Facet 4 is a null, and it is in the world
`FrI.tsv` has **no f series and no g series at all** — s/p/d only to n = 30, stated in its own header. Not our gap; the data has not been published. Ra I is on disk but its Rydberg electron sees a Ra⁺(7s) core, not Rn, so its f channel (1.14629) must not be read across that boundary. **The only remaining route is Ra II's nf series** — that is now the entire justification for going outside, and it is one query.

### The isolate
`ISOLATE-LOWDIN-3.tar.gz` — **40 KB, 14 files, verified against its own manifest.** It carries the seven heavy-element level tables, the full store, `store_gen.py`, the 1,287 non-computed index rows, and this session's findings and script. `store_gen` runs with the isolate root as cwd. **No restore point is needed next session** — upload this instead of the 14 MB bank.

Owed to the writing chat, added to the collision list: facets 1 ≡ 4 under the diagonal map; the 43-species population and its two domains; the δ(d)-collapse association at 41/43; facet 5 at the Rn core; facet 4 as a published-data null; the second promotion failure.
